dse_runs.notes: Spec: 16-axis motor control, 32 requests per 1us tick, all results back within 0.44us p99. Need throughput >= 32 Msps and tight batch latency. Pipelined families (pipelined, pipelined_m) are the natural fit for high throughput with small area; unrolled_k with k>=32 could also meet the batch deadline but may cost area. Keep max_abs_err <= 2^-12 (accuracy_bits >= 12). Minimize luts+ffs.

final_text: Campaign complete. The single spec **multiaxis_control** (16-axis motor control, 32 requests per 1 µs tick, p99 batch ≤ 0.44 µs, error ≤ 2⁻¹², minimize LUTs+FFs) was taken down the full ladder: L1 used all 400 evaluations via the structured DSE graph (refine → refine → stop), producing a 24-design feasible Pareto front dominated by pipelined_m m=4 designs; L2 SimPy simulation of the top 5 confirmed the batch latency (simulated p99 0.395 µs, passing the 0.44 µs constraint) with no winner change; L3/L4/L5 found no recorded verification, synthesis, or measured data for the selected design, so back_annotate returned `no_measured_data` and no reexplore was needed. Final selection: **pipelined_m (data_width=18, n_iter=14, angle_guard=1, frac_guard=1, rounding=trunc, m=4)** — 1161 LUTs+FFs (868 LUT / 293 FF), 12.5-bit accuracy (max error 2⁻¹²·⁵), 93.6 Msps throughput, simulated p99 batch latency 0.395 µs — all constraints satisfied.
